contexts.text: The curtains upon the habitation of the tent were to be made of she-goat's wool (), for a sign that all the holy things which were therein represented, derived their essence from innocence. The she-goat's wool = the ultimate or outermost of innocence, which is in ignorance, such as there is with the gentiles, who, in the internal sense, are the curtains of the tabernacle.
The curtains which were around represented natural things, which are external.

Ten curtains () = all the truths of which it consists. Curtains, or curtains = the interior truths of faith which belong to the new Intellectual; for the habitation = the Second Heaven, which is Heaven from the reception of Divine truth from the Lord's Divine good; therefore the curtains with which it was constructed and covered = the truths of faith which belong to the new Intellectual: the reason they = interior truths, is that exterior truths are signified by the curtains of goat's wool for the tent which was round about.
That curtains or curtains = the truths of faith which belong to those who are in the Lord's Spiritual Kingdom. Illustrated.
Curtain = the interior truth of faith which belongs to the new Intellectual. AC 9604.
One curtain = so in each of the truths. AC 9619.

Five curtains shall there be joined together, each to the other, and five curtains joined together, each to the other () = the constant communication of truth with good, and of good with truth... for the communications must be reciprocal, in order that there may be a conjugial conjunction of truth and good. Explained.

Thou shalt make curtains from goats for the tent upon the habitation () = the external of Heaven which is from the truths that are from external celestial good. Curtains = the interior truths of faith; here, the exterior truths of faith, because they were for the tent that was upon the habitation.
Curtain = truth from external celestial good. AC 9627.
The Word in the sense of the letter... is also meant by the curtains and veils of the tabernacle. DSS 46, General article.

Hence it follows, that by the ultimates of the tabernacle, which were the curtains and veils, thus its coverings and containants, are signified the ultimates of the Word, which are the truths and goods of the sense of its letter. Because these were signified, all the curtains and veils were made of fine linen interwoven, and of hyacinthine and crimson, and scarlet double-dyed, with cherubs... In the Arcana Coelestia it is shown that the curtains and veils represent the externals of Heaven and the Church, thus also the externals of the Word... DSS 97:3. TCR 220.
Under the roof, high above the table, there appeared a wide-spread canopy, shining with precious stones...
A theatre, on which there hangs a painted curtain.
Curtains () = natural truths from a spiritual origin; and to make and weave them = to teach.
